chunks: From him (Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad) from Ibn Ribat from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man had a debt of fifteen wasqs of dates owed to him by another man, and the debtor had a date palm grove. The creditor said to him, "Take what is in my palm grove in exchange for your dates," but the debtor refused to accept. So the creditor went to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so owes me fifteen wasqs of dates; ask him to take what is in my palm grove in exchange for his dates." The Prophet sent to him and said, "O so-and-so, take what is in his palm grove in exchange for your dates." He said, "O Messenger of Allah, it will not be sufficient (in quality/quantity)," and he refused to do so. The Messenger of Allah said to the owner of the palm grove, "Cut your palm trees." So he cut them, and he weighed out for him fifteen wasqs.'

So some of our companions informed me from Ibn Ribat, and I do not know except that I heard it from him, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When Rabī'ah al-Ra'yī heard this from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he said, "This is riba (usury)." I said, "I bear witness by Allah that he is among the liars." He said, "He was truthful."'

key_terms.رَبِيعَةَ الرَّأْيِ: Rabī'ah al-Ra'yī, a prominent jurist known for his independent reasoning
key_terms.وَسْقاً: A unit of volume/weight for dry goods, typically dates or grain

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging dates for a date palm grove to settle a debt according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *qiyas* (analogy) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates Rabī'ah al-Ra'yī’s reasoning that exchanging a specific quantity of dates for a different form of value (palm grove) without immediate full settlement constitutes *riba*. The narrative highlights the Prophet’s directive to liquidate the asset (cutting the trees) to ensure precise measurement, reinforcing the prohibition of *riba al-fadl* and *riba al-nasi'ah* in commodity exchanges. It serves as a foundational precedent for distinguishing between valid trade and usurious transactions involving foodstuffs.
